In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the echocardiography of acute myocarditis is characterized by the following: (1) regional contraction abnormalities, (2) hyperkinesia in the uninvolved regions, (3) "quivering" in the hypokinetic regions, (4) fibrosis and (5) dilatation of the left ventricle.
the echocardiographic findings in infectious myocarditis correlate well with the clinical and electrocardio- graphic manifestations of the disease.
the echocardiography in infectious myocarditis is useful in the diagnosis, prognosis and management of the disease.

we were able to demonstrate the presence of regional asynergia in patients with acute infectious myocarditis.
we have shown that the clinical course of acute infectious myocarditis can be predicted by echo findings.
in patients with infectious myocarditis the echocardiogram can be useful in determining the severity of disease and in predicting the outcome.

echocardiography is a very useful tool in the diagnosis of myocarditis.
in acute myocarditis, the site and extent of wall motion abnormalities correlate with the clinical severity of disease, and that the asynergia is often accompanied by a "quivering" echo pattern.
